gitCommit.body:
Do not take the folders Claude Code creates for tampering with the kit (#48)

* Close the remaining gaps of the security review: approvers, tests of other tickets, test setup

The review of the kit's security found, besides the two gaps fixed in the
previous change, three more that need no model call.

1. Approval. GitHub's author association says that someone belongs to the
   repository, not what they may do there: a member or a collaborator can
   have read access only, whereas GitHub's own required reviews ignore
   them. A request for changes from any account blocked QA verify, though
   their approval would not have counted.
   - qa/ci-permissions.sh reads each reviewer's permission
     (collaborators/{login}/permission); qa/github-approval.ts counts an
     approval only with write access or more, and a request for changes
     only from someone whose approval would count.
   - The permissions only narrow: a login that cannot be read falls back to
     the association and the job warns, so the kit works as before where
     the token may not read them. Whether the workflows' token may is not
     confirmed: the documentation could not be read from this session.

2. Tests of a ticket that a pull request does not name, and the QA agent
   rewriting existing tests. qa/check-test-blocks.ts reads test files test
   by test (it, test, hooks), with a scanner that skips strings, templates,
   comments and regular expressions: 294 tests in the repository's 56 test
   files, none left open.
   - A pull request may not change, remove or move a test whose title
     carries [TICKET-N][AC-N] of a ticket it does not name. It runs on
     every pull request in QA branch rules, also for tickets whose qa/
     branch was deleted.
   - A QA branch may add tests and rewrite its own ticket's, not another
     ticket's test, a test with no ticket, or a hook that was there. It
     runs in check-scope.sh scope, before the push in QA write tests and
     QA amend tests, and on the pull request.

3. Test setup. The repair agent could edit src/setupTests.ts,
   vitest.setup.ts, mocks and helpers.
   - The guard refuses them by name (isSupportFile in check-tooling.ts and
     the same two patterns in qa-guard.sh; a test keeps them in step).
   - tooling-integrity.ts adds package.json, the test configuration, the
     setup files it names and what those import, and the files that are
     test support by name to the snapshot compared after every repair
     step, so a change made by code that the tests run is caught too.
   - QA verify also names a pull request's changes to such files.

Regression tests for each rule, on real git histories, and a mutation
check that the test for imported helpers fails without the import
closure. npm run check: 270 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped (the same three
as on main, which need a full clone, bwrap and npm ci in the demo). Not
run on a GitHub-hosted runner. Limits are in SECURITY.md.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01N4hLdLD4m4sZNjEADxtoct

* Do not take the folders Claude Code creates for tampering with the kit

The first real run of QA write tests after the integrity checks (GitHub
runner, TICKET-44 on the demo shop, Claude Code 2.1.303): the writer
finished (verdict ready, 10 turns, 56 s, $0.14, red tests for both
criteria), then qa/run-qa.sh stopped with "the kit's own files changed
while the agent ran (.claude/, .claude/.cc-writes/, .claude/agents/,
.claude/commands/)".

Claude Code had created those empty folders in the project while it
started its session. The manifest of qa/kit-integrity.sh listed folders,
so an empty one that appeared counted as a change, and the run could
never go on in an application with no .claude/ of its own (and very
likely not in one at the root either). Only folders were listed in the
log, no file: a file would have been named.

The manifest now lists files, links and what is neither, not folders. A
file created inside a new folder is still reported. The tests could not
show it: the stand-in for claude created nothing. The new ones create
what the runner showed, in the application-at-the-root layout, in the
kit-outside-the-project layout with no .claude/ in the project, and in
the repair loop; with the previous script they fail (4 of 26).

qa/ci-write-tests.sh publish had no test, and it is the step that runs
next, with the scope check added in the previous change. It now runs on
a real git history with a bare origin and a stand-in for gh: added tests
are committed and pushed with feat/<ticket> and the pull request, a test
added to a shared file is accepted, a rewrite of another ticket's test
or of a test with no ticket stops the run before anything is pushed.

npm run check: 277 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped (the same three as on
main). The touched test files also pass as an unprivileged user. Not
run again on a runner.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01N4hLdLD4m4sZNjEADxtoct
